question: A range officer wants the combined thrust, in N, of 2 identical booster stacks, each built from 12 identical motors, so first find one motor's net thrust. A test mass of 116 kg is mounted on a motor; from t = 2 s to t = 3 s the motor's acceleration grows at a rate of 5t² + 3t (in m/s³, with t in seconds), starting from zero acceleration at t = 2 s. The motor's raw thrust is the force needed to give the 116 kg mass the acceleration reached at t = 3 s. From that raw thrust subtract 20 N of aerodynamic drag, and then subtract a further 23 N of rail friction, to obtain one motor's net thrust. The test rail is 640 m long. What is the combined thrust of the 2 stacks, in N?

A maintenance trolley of mass 55000 g is pushed along a level factory floor with an acceleration a, in m/s², that satisfies a² − 5a + 4 = 0; the larger of the two possible values is the one actually achieved. The push on one such trolley is exactly the force needed to give it that acceleration. A train of 11 identical trolleys is coupled together and each receives the same push, so the total applied force is 11 times the single-trolley push. Of that total, 29 N is absorbed by the couplings and then a further 4 N by a dragging brake shoe. Express the force that remains, in kN.

A crane operator tests a load whose mass is 179000 g. The load's acceleration, in m/s², is set by a dial code built in stages: start with the largest whole number that divides both 54 and 149 exactly, multiply it by 4, multiply the result by 7, and finally add 29. The hoist cable is 40 m long. The extra cable tension is the force needed to give the 179000 g load that acceleration. The crane performs 10 identical lifts in a shift, and the operator adds up that force over all 10 lifts. What is the summed force, in N?

The figure the technician needs is a net energy in J, found from the following account. The energy of motion of 12 identical pucks is totalled, 21 J of that total is lost to friction on the air table, and then 15 J is added by a final tap of the launcher. Each puck has a mass of 44 kg and slides at a speed, in m/s, equal to the largest whole number that divides both 383 and 310 with no remainder. Compute one puck's energy of motion first and scale up to the 12 pucks before applying the loss and the addition. What is the net energy, in J?

A quality inspector's final report figure is an energy in kJ: the output of a whole press line plus 3 kJ of standby energy. The press line has 9 identical presses, and each press holds 3 identical hammers. Each hammer has a mass of 8 kg and strikes at a speed, in m/s, equal to the sum of the terms 2k − 1 for k running from 1 to 6. A press's output is the energy of motion of its 3 hammers combined, and the line's output is the 9 presses combined, converted to kJ. What is the report figure, in kJ?

The plant manager wants the total energy of motion, in kJ, of an entire fleet: 5 identical trucks, each towing 3 identical loaded pallet-trailers. Each trailer has a mass of 44 kg on the test scale and moves at a speed, in m/s, equal to 6 times the sum of 5 and 4. Work out one trailer's energy of motion and express it in kJ, combine the 3 trailers of one truck, and then combine the 5 trucks. What is the fleet total, in kJ?

The quantity to find is a final energy reading in kJ, obtained by taking one probe's energy of motion in kJ, subtracting 2 kJ of instrument overhead, and multiplying by 4 because 4 identical probes are launched. Each probe has a mass of 51000 g. From t = 1 s to t = 2 s a probe's acceleration, in m/s², follows 2t² + 8t with t in seconds, and the probe is at rest at t = 1 s. The probe's energy of motion is taken at its speed at t = 2 s. What is the final reading, in kJ?

The number needed is the total energy of motion, in J, across an entire delivery: 5 identical vans, each carrying 7 identical racks, each rack holding 9 identical parcels. Every parcel has a mass of 52000 g, and on the conveyor each parcel moves at a speed, in m/s, equal to the largest whole number that divides both 355 and 183 with no remainder. Find the energy of motion of one parcel, then of one rack, then of one van, and then of the whole delivery. What is that total, in J?

A bottling plant's conveyor pushes crates, each of mass 16 kg, with an acceleration, in m/s², equal to the number of ways of choosing 2 bottles from a row of 10. The force on one crate is what is required to produce that acceleration. A line carries 11 crates at once, so the line's force is 11 times the single-crate force; express it in kN. The motor controller then adds a bias of 15 kN to the line's force. The plant runs 5 identical lines, and the supervisor totals the biased line forces. What is that total, in kN?

The quantity to report is a net signed force in kN, with forward taken as positive: one cart's forward driving force in kN, minus 16 kN of opposing retarder force, multiplied by 5 because 5 identical carts share the retarder, plus 3 kN of forward assist from a booster. Each cart has a mass of 63000 g and is driven with an acceleration a, in m/s², where a is the larger of the two values satisfying a² − 9a + 20 = 0. The driving force on a cart is whatever is required to give it that acceleration. What is the net signed force, in kN?

The value to report is a net energy balance in kJ, with energy gained counted positive and energy spent counted negative: one cart's energy of motion in kJ, minus 30 kJ spent by the launcher's compressor, multiplied by 3 because 3 identical carts are launched, plus 11 kJ recovered by a regenerative brake. Each cart has a mass of 12000 g. The cart starts from rest at t = 2 s, and from t = 2 s to t = 3 s its acceleration, in m/s², is 1t² + 6t, with t in seconds; its energy of motion is taken at its speed at t = 3 s. The launch track is 15 m long. What is the net energy balance, in kJ?

The figure wanted is a final net force in N: the combined drive force of 12 identical rail carriages, plus 28 N supplied by a helper spring, minus 12 N of rail friction. Each carriage has a mass of 62000 g, and its position along the straight track is 3t³ − 3t² metres, with t in seconds. The drive force on one carriage is whatever is needed to give it the acceleration it has at t = 3 s. Add the 12 carriages' drive forces before applying the spring and the friction. What is the final net force, in N?

At a parcel depot, every bin has a mass of 28 kg and rides the sorting conveyor at a speed, in m/s, equal to 2 times the sum of 6 and 15. Find the energy of motion of one bin and express it in kJ. A trolley's load is 3 such bins, a van's load is 5 such trolleys, and the depot dispatches 10 such vans. Scale the single-bin figure up to a trolley, then to a van, then to the 10 vans. What is the total energy of motion of all the bins, in kJ?

The number to report is a total energy in kJ for 6 identical racks, each rack holding 5 identical carts, where each cart's contribution is its energy of motion in kJ less 5 kJ of standby heating. A cart has a mass of 20 kg and runs on a rail 12 m long. The cart starts from rest at t = 2 s, and from t = 2 s to t = 4 s its acceleration, in m/s², is 1t² + 5t with t in seconds; its energy of motion is taken at its speed at t = 4 s. What is the total for the 6 racks, in kJ?

The final figure required is a force reading in kN: the combined thrust of 7 identical actuators, converted to kN, plus a 1 kN preload from the test rig. Each actuator drives a 189 kg carriage. The carriage's acceleration, in m/s², is 3 times the sum of 9 and 9, less 9. The thrust of one actuator is the force needed to give the carriage that acceleration. The rig's hydraulic reservoir holds 40 L. What is the force reading, in kN?

A model rocket of mass 42000 g is at rest at t = 1 s, and from t = 1 s to t = 2 s its acceleration, in m/s², is 1t² + 3t with t in seconds. The launch pad stands 1.5 m above the ground. Take the rocket's energy of motion at its speed at t = 2 s, add the 28 J delivered by a final puff of the ejection charge, and subtract 6 J lost to air drag. The club launches 10 identical rockets this way and adds their results together, then subtracts 3 J for a timing-circuit loss. What is the resulting energy, in J?

The quantity to find is a total force in kN: the combined force of 7 identical hoists, converted to kN, plus a 1 kN reading offset. Each hoist raises 10 identical crates, each of mass 54 kg, and gives each crate an acceleration a, in m/s², where a is the smaller of the two values satisfying a² − 7a + 6 = 0. The force on one crate is what is required to produce that acceleration, a hoist's force is the combined force on its 10 crates, and the 7 hoists' forces are combined. What is the total, in kN?

The value wanted is a total energy in kJ for 5 identical test days. On each day, 12 identical launches are made, and each launch fires 12 identical projectiles; the day's total is the energy of motion of all its projectiles, expressed in kJ. A projectile has a mass of 47 kg and leaves at a speed, in m/s, equal to the sum of k for k running from 1 to 9. The launcher's rail is inclined at 30°. Find one projectile's energy of motion, scale it to a launch, then to a day, then to the 5 days. What is the total, in kJ?

The result to report is a total force in kN, obtained by adding 17 N, then 10 N, then 16 N to the drive force on a cart and converting the sum to kN. The cart has a mass of 59 kg and is 0.8 m long. Its acceleration a, in m/s², is the smaller of the two values satisfying a² − 8a + 12 = 0, and the drive force is what is needed to produce that acceleration. What is the total force, in kN?

A lab technician wants a final energy balance in kJ: the energy of motion of a flywheel test mass, expressed in kJ, minus 22 kJ dissipated in the bearings, plus 27 kJ fed in by the motor. The test mass is 11 kg and moves at a speed, in m/s, equal to the sum of k for k running from 1 to 6. Compute its energy of motion first, then apply the loss and the input in that order. What is the final balance, in kJ?

A ballistic pendulum on a lab bench uses a bob of mass 46 kg hung on a 2.0 m wire. The launcher's speed setting, in m/s, is numerically equal to the rate at which the slope of the curve y = 3x³ + 0x² is itself changing at x = 1. Find the bob's energy of motion at that speed and double it for the 2 bobs used. Subtract the 8 J lost in the release catch, and then multiply by 11 for the 11 trials in the series. What is the total, in J?

The number to find is a final force in N: the combined force on 6 identical wagons, plus 19 N from a spring, plus a further 13 N from a second spring, plus another 19 N from a third spring. Each wagon has a mass of 154000 g and its acceleration a, in m/s², is the larger of the two values satisfying a² − 10a + 16 = 0. The force on one wagon is what is required to give it that acceleration. The yard is at 12 °C. What is the final force, in N?

A pneumatic launcher fires a puck of mass 29000 g. The puck starts from rest at t = 2 s, and from t = 2 s to t = 3 s its acceleration, in m/s², is 4t² + 2t with t in seconds. Take the puck's energy of motion at its speed at t = 3 s. A magazine holds 12 pucks and the launcher has 6 magazines, all fired identically, so scale the energy to 12 pucks and then to 6 magazines. Finally subtract 8 J of latch friction and add 22 J from the compressor's residual charge. What is the resulting energy, in J?

The value a wind-tunnel crew must report is a signed energy balance in kJ, with energy gained positive: one carriage's energy of motion in kJ, minus 5 kJ spent by the drive motor, minus 10 kJ spent by the cooling fans, all multiplied by 5 because 5 identical carriages are run. Each carriage has a mass of 34 kg and travels at a speed v, in m/s, where v is the larger of the two values satisfying v² − 13v + 42 = 0. What is the balance, in kJ?

The total the range officer wants is an energy in J across 11 identical firing sessions; each session's figure is the energy of motion of 5 identical darts plus 30 J from a spring loader. A dart has a mass of 4 kg and its fin span is 12 cm. A dart starts from rest at t = 0 s and from t = 0 s to t = 4 s its acceleration, in m/s², is 3t² + 0t with t in seconds; a headwind then takes 5 m/s off its speed at t = 4 s, and the energy of motion is taken at the reduced speed. What is the total, in J?
